reviews.text: Excellent veterinary center, trained, competent, and very professional medical staff. My poodle broke a leg and they referred me to an excellent orthopedic surgeon (thanks to Dr. Adalgisa who recommended the orthopedic surgeon and the clinic where I could take him). He had to operate on him to place screws and a plate. The clinic staff looked after me at all times, right from the start, both post-op and aftercare. I highly recommend it.

I'm happy to share my extremely positive experience.
Dr. Cinzia immediately showed great empathy for me (which is not to be taken for granted), and for my new little 3-month-old dog, it was precious for us to meet someone so attentive and capable in her work.
She was able to immediately understand the causes and RESOLVE the problems Nala was experiencing twice. Being a dog found in the countryside, her conditions weren't the best, but with the doctor's help, everything got better and better!
Furthermore, since I don't live in Rome, but was only passing through, she was always available to accommodate our needs, such as rescheduling her booster vaccination to meet our needs.
We are certain that, in addition to holding her in our hearts, we will return to visit her, to renew our THANK YOU and show her how much we have grown.

My cat Zorba was treated at this clinic only for the last two years of his life (due to our move to this area), but I can only leave a positive review. Specifically, I want to thank Dr. Strappa, who always treated him with great patience and availability, despite his "difficult" nature. She was the only doctor who came close to the correct diagnosis (which was also the cause of his death). The clinic has obvious limitations (it's not a clinic, and there are no specialists, and there aren't any more sophisticated machines—MRIs, CT scans, etc.)—but as far as we could, Zorba was always well cared for, unlike other larger, more renowned clinics where, unfortunately, his condition was treated very superficially, ultimately leading to his death.
I therefore thank Dr. Strappa, our "general practitioner," and I give a special mention to Dr. Ciocci, because on the day of Zorba's first ischemic attack (a Saturday morning), even though I didn't have an appointment and we were in an emergency room, didn't hesitate to see him right away, performing all the tests he could and a visit worthy of a neurologist. I really appreciated that he spoke to me empathetically but clearly about my cat's serious condition. Despite the pain, communication is also a tool for coping with the most dire situations. Thank you!
